name: Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS)
description: Monthly and annual-average civilian labor force, employment, unemployment and unemployment rate by place of residence for about 8,300 areas (Census regions and divisions, states, metros, counties, cities of 25,000+, New England cities and towns). States are model-based and benchmarked to national CPS; substate areas use Handbook and ACS-share disaggregation.
access_requirements: Descriptive User-Agent header required. Tab-delimited text with CRLF line ends and space-padded fields (series_id right-padded; value left-padded). la.data.64.County (336 MB) and la.data.65.City (330 MB) are large; per-state files la.data.7 to la.data.59 (e.g., la.data.21.Indiana, 18.8 MB) hold all areas in one state.
geo_levels: region;division;state;cbsa;csa;county;place;cousub;other:metropolitan divisions;other:small labor market areas;other:city parts by county;other:balance of state
time_coverage: Monthly Jan 1976- for states, DC, Puerto Rico, Census regions/divisions, New York city and Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale MD; Jan 1990- for counties, metros and most cities (cities added when they pass 25,000); latest Aug 2026 (states) and Jul 2026 (substate); annual averages (period M13) for not seasonally adjusted series through 2025
update_cadence: Monthly; annual processing each spring revises up to 5 prior years (by mid-April)
history_notes: 2nd-generation models 1994; 3rd-generation models and real-time benchmarking to CPS 2005; 4th-generation models 2015 (states re-estimated to 1976, substate revised back to 2010); Mar 2025: OMB 2023 delineations, NECTAs dropped, CT 9 planning regions replace 8 counties back to 1990, intercensal population controls (removing a Dec-2016/Jan-2017 wedge break); Oct 2025 not collected (lapse in appropriations); 2025 annual averages are 11-month averages (footnote G).
suppression_rules: No confidentiality suppression. Missing values are '-' with footnote codes (X = 2025 lapse in appropriations; U = annual average cannot be calculated; N = not available); P = preliminary.
limitations: Substate figures are not direct survey estimates; cities and city parts are disaggregated from counties using ACS shares; no demographic detail; counties and cities are not seasonally adjusted; national totals are not in the LA database (use CPS LN series); levels are persons (CPS levels are thousands).
doc_evidence: Fetched la.txt (file list, formats, M13 = annual average, about 8,300 areas), LAUS FAQ, Handbook of Methods calculation/history pages and 'LAUS Geography and Data Changes in 2025'.
sample_evidence: Downloaded la.area (8,351 areas), la.series (33,985 series), la.data.21.Indiana (18.8 MB): LAUCN180890000000003 2025 M13 = 5.1 (footnote G); Oct 2025 value '-' (X).

name: Current Population Survey labor force statistics (LN database)
description: National monthly household-survey estimates of labor force status (unemployment rate, participation, employment-population ratio) with demographic detail; the national counterpart to LAUS, whose state not seasonally adjusted estimates are controlled to CPS national totals.
access_requirements: Descriptive User-Agent required. ln.data.1.AllData is about 390 MB and sorted by series_id (HTTP range requests work). BLS Public Data API v1 answered without a key but returned no M13 annual averages.
time_coverage: Monthly 1948- (LNS14000000); annual averages 1947- (LNU04000000 M13); latest Aug 2026
update_cadence: Monthly (Employment Situation); annual averages with December data; seasonally adjusted data revised for 5 years each January
history_notes: New population controls each January (e.g., January 2026, footnote 12); Oct 2025 not collected and Q4 2025 averages not produced; 2025 annual averages are 11-month averages excluding October (footnote 11).
suppression_rules: Footnote 7 marks data that do not meet publication criteria; '-' for unavailable data.
limitations: Levels are in thousands; national only in this source; standard errors exist only for some series (ln.aspect).
doc_evidence: Fetched ln.txt (counts in thousands, rates one decimal, M13 = annual average), ln.series (LNU04000000 begins 1947 M13) and ln.footnote (codes 9-12 for the 2025 lapse).
sample_evidence: Range requests into ln.data.1.AllData: LNU04000000 2024 M13 = 4.0; 2025 M13 = 4.3 (footnote 11); 2025 M10 '-' (footnote 9).

name: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW)
description: Near-universe administrative counts of establishments, monthly employment and quarterly and annual wages for jobs covered by state unemployment insurance (UI) and federal UCFE programs, by NAICS industry (to 6 digits) and ownership, tabulated by worksite location (workplace-based).
access_requirements: Descriptive User-Agent required. Area slices exist only for 2014 onward (1990-2013 return 404; use annual_by_area zip files). Area codes: county FIPS (18089), state SS000 (18000), U.S. US000, MSA C plus first 4 CBSA digits (C1242), CSA CS### (CS176).
time_coverage: NAICS-based 1990-2025 annual and quarterly (county data through 2026 Q1); NAICS files for 1975-1989 contain only ownership totals; SIC-based 1975-2000; open-data slices 2014-
history_notes: NAICS data for 1990-2000 were reconstructed from SIC-coded data; beginning 2025 Q2 MSA data are published as totals only (the 2025 annual MSA slice has one data row); Connecticut: 8 counties through 2023, 9 planning regions (09110-09190) from 2024.
suppression_rules: disclosure_code 'N' = not disclosed; suppressed employment and wage fields appear as 0 while establishment counts can still show; separate lq_disclosure_code and oty_disclosure_code.
limitations: Counts jobs (not people) where the establishment is located; limited to UI/UCFE-covered employment; multi-establishment reporting and industry reclassification can shift local industry counts; location quotients are relative to the U.S.
doc_evidence: Fetched QCEW CSV Data Slices page (URL pattern, move to data.bls.gov), annual slice layout page (disclosure codes) and QCEW overview (MSA totals-only change from 2025 Q2).
sample_evidence: Annual slices 2024 and 2025 for 18089 (1,769 and 1,773 rows): 2025 total covered employment 191,579; average annual pay 62,399; 786 rows flagged N.

name: Current Employment Statistics - State and Area (CES)
description: Monthly establishment-survey estimates of nonfarm payroll jobs, hours and earnings by industry for states and about 450 metropolitan and other labor areas (including metropolitan divisions); workplace-based; benchmarked annually using QCEW employment.
access_requirements: Descriptive User-Agent required. series_id = SM + S/U + state (2) + area (5) + industry (8) + data type (2); per-state data files (e.g., sm.data.15.Indiana, 14 MB).
time_coverage: Total nonfarm from 1939 for states; most metro and industry series from Jan 1990; latest Aug 2026; annual averages (M13)
history_notes: Annual benchmark revisions; metro definitions follow OMB delineations; sm.txt describes 2012 NAICS classification.
suppression_rules: Series published only where the sample supports them; no county-level estimates.
limitations: Jobs counted at establishment location (not residents); excludes self-employed and farm jobs; employment in thousands.
doc_evidence: Fetched sm.txt: SM survey definition, about 450 major labor areas, total nonfarm from 1939, most other series from January 1990, employment in thousands.
sample_evidence: sm.data.15.Indiana: SMU18294140000000001 (Lake County-Porter County-Jasper County IN Metro Division, total nonfarm) 2025 M13 = 285.1 thousand.

name: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS)
description: Annual (May reference) employer-survey estimates of employment and wage distributions (mean and 10th-90th percentiles) for detailed occupations by nation, state, metropolitan area and nonmetropolitan area; workplace-based.
access_requirements: Descriptive User-Agent required; oe.data.0.Current (331 MB) and oe.series (1.26 GB) are large; series_id = OE + U + area type + area (7) + industry (6) + occupation (6) + data type (2).
time_coverage: Only the current release is in the time.series files: May 2025 (oe.release 2025A01)
history_notes: Estimates pool six semiannual panels (three years) with older wages aged to the current May; occupation and area definitions change periodically.
suppression_rules: Footnote 8 'Estimate not released'; wages at or above $115.00/hour or $239,200/year are top-coded (footnote 5); relative standard errors published (data types 02, 05).
limitations: Excludes self-employed; BLS cautions that the design limits time-series use; no county estimates.
doc_evidence: Fetched OEWS FAQ: three years of data (six panels), limited time-series usefulness, excludes self-employed, national/state/MSA/nonmetropolitan coverage.
sample_evidence: Range request of oe.data.0.Current: OEUM001018000000000000001 (all-occupation employment, Abilene TX) 2025 A01 = 75070; oe.release = May 2025.

name: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U)
description: Monthly consumer price index; U.S. city average all items, not seasonally adjusted, series CUUR0000SA0 (1982-84=100) with annual average in period M13; also regional, division and metro-area indexes.
access_requirements: Descriptive User-Agent required. CUUR0000SA0 is also in cu.data.0.Current and cu.data.2.Summaries.
time_coverage: Monthly Jan 1913 to Aug 2026 (CUUR0000SA0); annual averages 1913-2025
update_cadence: Monthly (typically the 10th-14th of the following month)
history_notes: Methodology improvements are not applied retroactively (use R-CPI-U-RS for a consistent research series); Oct 2025 index not published (footnote X); the 2025 annual average (321.943) equals the mean of the 11 available months.
suppression_rules: None; '-' with footnote X for Oct 2025.
limitations: Area indexes show change over time only, not price-level differences between areas; Census recommends R-CPI-U-RS rather than CPI-U for ACS income comparisons across years.
doc_evidence: Fetched cu.txt (file list, SA0 in AllItems and Summaries, base 1982-84, annual averages for unadjusted series) and the BLS 2025 shutdown CPI impact page.

name: R-CPI-U-RS: Consumer Price Index Retroactive Series using current methods (formerly CPI-U-RS)
description: Research price index estimating the CPI-U from 1978 as if current methods had been used throughout; monthly values and annual averages (December 1977 = 100). Census uses it to inflation-adjust ACS dollar estimates across years.
access_requirements: Single XLSX (sheet 'All items'; header row 6: YEAR, JAN-DEC, AVG; note row after 2025).
time_coverage: 1978-2025 monthly and annual average (AVG column); December 1977 = 100
update_cadence: Annual (published once a year in March)
history_notes: Values can change at each annual update (BLS posted incorrect values on Mar 31, 2026 and corrected them in April 2026); Oct 2025 unavailable but the 2025 AVG is populated (474.994); differences from CPI-U are large before 1999.
suppression_rules: None.
limitations: Research series with extrapolated adjustments; national only; Census 2024 guidance factor 1.02937903 (2023 to 2024) differs slightly from the ratio of the current XLSX annual averages (1.02948), so record the vintage used.
doc_evidence: Fetched R-CPI-U-RS homepage: estimates CPI-U from 1978, published once a year in March, correction notice, link 'All items, 1977-2025 (XLSX)'.

name: BEA Regional Accounts: county personal income (CAINC1, CAINC4, CAINC5N, CAINC30)
description: Annual county personal income (residence-adjusted), BEA midyear population, per capita personal income, income components (net earnings, dividends/interest/rent, transfer receipts), earnings by place of work and earnings by NAICS industry.
access_requirements: Zip files need no key. BEA API requires a free 36-character UserID (limits 100 requests/min, 100 MB/min, 30 errors/min). Nonexistent zip names return an HTML error page with status 200, so check Content-Type.
geo_levels: nation;state;county;other:BEA regions (8);other:Virginia county-independent city combination areas
time_coverage: 1969-2024 (CAINC1, CAINC4, CAINC30); 2001-2024 NAICS industry earnings (CAINC5N); SIC industry earnings for earlier years in CAINC5S
update_cadence: Annual (2024 county statistics released Feb 5, 2026 with revisions to 2020-2023)
history_notes: Connecticut: 8 counties 1969-2023 and 9 planning regions for 2024 only (no overlap); Alaska area changes (1979, 1988, 1991, 1993, 2008, 2009, 2013, 2020); Broomfield CO from 2002; Menominee WI separate from 1989; NAICS industry detail from 2001; metro and other county-aggregate statistics discontinued; county employment table CAEMP25N ended with 2022 data.
suppression_rules: (NA) not available; (NM) not meaningful; (D) not shown to avoid disclosure but included in higher-level totals (industry tables such as CAINC5N and CAGDP2); (L) not observed in current county files.
limitations: Current dollars only; per capita uses the population vintage of each release; independent cities under 100,000 (1980) combined with adjacent Virginia counties; Kalawao HI combined with Maui; the BEA U.S. total is the sum of states and DC and differs from NIPA personal income.
doc_evidence: Fetched BEA download page and zip-list JSON, CAINC1 footnotes/definition XML (lines 1-3), FAQ 105 (state total vs NIPA), FAQ 1481 (aggregates dropped), BEA API user guide.
sample_evidence: CAINC1.zip (3.47 MB): CAINC1__ALL_AREAS_1969_2024.csv, 9,627 rows, 3,209 areas; Lake County IN (18089) 2024 per capita personal income = 58,423.

name: BEA Regional Accounts: state annual personal income (SAINC tables)
description: Annual state personal income, population, per capita personal income and components (SAINC1, SAINC4, SAINC30 and other SAINC tables) for states, BEA regions and the United States.
access_url: https://apps.bea.gov/regional/zip/SAINC.zip (contains SAINC1__ALL_AREAS_1929_2025.csv and per-state files); https://apps.bea.gov/regional/zip/SAINC1.zip does not exist
access_requirements: No key for the zip; BEA API (datasetname=Regional, TableName=SAINC1) requires a UserID.
time_coverage: 1929-2025 annual (Alaska and Hawaii from 1950); quarterly state personal income in SQINC
update_cadence: Annual (2025 released Apr 9, 2026 with revisions to 2020-2024); quarterly (SQINC)
history_notes: Population vintage and recent years revised at each release.
suppression_rules: (NA) not available; (NM) not meaningful.
limitations: SAINC1 dollars are in millions (CAINC1 in thousands); population vintage differs from CAINC1 (2024 U.S. population 340,003,797 vs 340,110,988), so do not mix releases without recording vintage.
doc_evidence: Fetched BEA zip-list JSON (SAINC = Annual Personal Income by State; no SAINC1 zip) and read SAINC1 footnotes from the zip.
sample_evidence: SAINC.zip (17.5 MB, 1,017 files): SAINC1__ALL_AREAS_1929_2025.csv; U.S. 2025 per capita personal income = 76,393; Indiana 2025 = 66,292.

name: BEA GDP by county (CAGDP1, CAGDP2, CAGDP9)
description: Annual county gross domestic product: real GDP in chained 2017 dollars, chain-type quantity index and current-dollar GDP (CAGDP1); current-dollar GDP by NAICS industry (CAGDP2); real GDP by industry (CAGDP9).
access_requirements: No key for the zips; BEA API requires a UserID.
time_coverage: 2001-2024 annual
history_notes: Connecticut planning regions from 2024 (8 counties earlier); metro-area GDP (county aggregates) discontinued; chained dollars use reference year 2017; Alaska, Broomfield and Virginia combination-area notes as in CAINC.
suppression_rules: (D) not shown to avoid disclosure (10,337 cells in the CAGDP2 Indiana file); (NA) not available; (NM) not meaningful.
limitations: Output is measured where production occurs (workplace-based); chained-dollar values are not additive across areas or industries; industry detail is heavily suppressed for small counties.
doc_evidence: Fetched BEA GDP by county page (Feb 5, 2026 release for 2024) and CAGDP1/CAGDP2 footnote files in the zips.
sample_evidence: CAGDP1.zip (1.9 MB): Lake County IN 2024 current-dollar GDP = 31,242,109 and real GDP = 24,764,214 (thousands of chained 2017 dollars).

name: BEA Regional Price Parities and real personal income (SARPP, MARPP, PARPP)
description: Regional Price Parities (price level relative to U.S. = 100) for all items, goods, housing, utilities and other services; implicit regional price deflators; state real personal income and real per capita personal income (SARPI).
access_requirements: No key for the zips; BEA API requires a UserID.
geo_levels: nation;state;cbsa;other:metro and nonmetro portions of states (PARPP)
time_coverage: 2008-2024 annual
update_cadence: Annual (2024 released Feb 19, 2026 with revisions to 2008-2023)
history_notes: Each release revises the 2008-forward series; metro areas follow current OMB delineations.
suppression_rules: (NA) where applicable.
limitations: Spatial price levels for a single year, not an inflation index; no county or place RPPs; metro real personal income not provided.
doc_evidence: Fetched BEA RPP page: RPPs measure price-level differences across states and metros for a given year; latest 2024 released Feb 19, 2026.
sample_evidence: SARPP.zip (39 KB) and MARPP.zip (146 KB): Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos MSA RPP all items 2024 = 98.066; Kansas City MSA = 92.543.

name: American Community Survey (ACS) detailed tables: employment, income, earnings, poverty, public assistance, industry and occupation
description: Continuous household survey; 1-year estimates for areas of 65,000+ population and 5-year estimates for all areas, many tables down to block groups; resident-based (industry and occupation describe residents' jobs wherever located).
access_requirements: Census API key (used by project adapter). Summary-file .dat files are pipe-delimited with GEO_ID and {TABLE}_E###/{TABLE}_M### columns (about 10-245 MB per table).
time_coverage: 1-year 2005-2024 (standard 2020 1-year not released); 5-year 2005-2009 through 2020-2024; 2025 1-year not yet on the API as of 2026-09-28
history_notes: 2020 1-year replaced by experimental estimates; dollars are in final-year inflation-adjusted dollars, so cross-period comparisons need R-CPI-U-RS factors; the 2024 geography file lists 9 Connecticut planning regions and no old counties.
suppression_rules: 90% margins of error published; 1-year estimates only for areas of 65,000+.
limitations: Sampling error is large for small areas; 5-year values are period estimates; Census comparison guidance pairs non-overlapping 5-year periods (e.g., 2015-2019 vs 2020-2024); some tables stop at tract (e.g., B17001, B17020, B22001, B19083, C24050).
doc_evidence: Fetched 2024 5-year table shells (5.6 MB; exact IDs and labels) and 'Comparing 2024 ACS Data' guidance (R-CPI-U-RS factors).
sample_evidence: Range requests of 2024 5-year summary files: B19013 U.S. = 80,734 (MOE 166); B19013, B23025, C24030 files contain block-group rows (1500000US...).

name: Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE): states and counties
description: Model-based annual estimates of people in poverty (all ages, ages 0-17, related children 5-17; ages 0-4 for states and nation only) and median household income, with 90% confidence intervals, combining ACS with administrative data.
access_requirements: Census API key for the API (project adapter). Bulk files are fixed-width text without a header row (layout: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/saipe/technical-documentation/file-layouts/state-county/2024-estimate-layout.txt).
time_coverage: 1989, 1993, 1995-2024 (states and counties); school districts 1995, 1997, 1999-2024 in a separate dataset
history_notes: 2004 to 2005 switch from CPS ASEC to ACS inputs (comparisons across the break not advised); ACS group quarters added 2006; counts not comparable across the 2010 census benchmark; Connecticut planning regions from 2022 (8 counties through 2021).
suppression_rules: None; all states and counties estimated; confidence intervals published.
limitations: Model-based with wide intervals for small counties; SAIPE and ACS are correlated so standard significance tests are conservative; county names truncated to 45 characters in text files.
doc_evidence: Fetched Census developer page (1989, 1993, 1995-2024), SAIPE cautions page, 2024 file layout, and API variables.json (SAEPOVRTALL_PT, SAEMHI_PT, _MOE, _LB90, _UB90).
sample_evidence: Downloaded est24-in.txt (24 KB): Lake County IN 2024 people in poverty 66,427 (13.3%, CI 11.8-14.8); median household income 73,228 (CI 70,499-75,957).

name: County Business Patterns (CBP) and ZIP Code Business Patterns (ZBP)
description: Annual establishments, mid-March employment, first-quarter and annual payroll by NAICS industry and employment-size class for employer establishments, by physical establishment location.
access_url: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cbp/datasets/{year}/cbp{yy}co.zip (also st, us, msa, csa, cd and zbp files); API: https://api.census.gov/data/{year}/cbp
access_requirements: None for bulk files; Census API key for the API (project adapter).
time_coverage: 1986-2023 files (NAICS from 1998, SIC earlier); 2023 released 2025-06-26; 2024 not yet on the API as of 2026-09-28
history_notes: SIC to NAICS in 1998 and later NAICS vintages (e.g., 2012 NAICS 2012-2016, 2017 NAICS 2017-2023); noise infusion since 2007; from 2017 cells with fewer than 3 establishments are not published and flag D was replaced by S; Connecticut planning regions in the 2022 and 2023 county files.
suppression_rules: Noise flags on EMP, QP1, AP: G (under 2%), H (2 to under 5%), J (5% or more); size-class value N = not available or not comparable; cells with fewer than 3 establishments withheld (2017+).
limitations: Excludes self-employed, private households, railroads, agricultural production and most government; employment is a mid-March snapshot; Commerce DAO 216-26 (2026) prohibits noise infusion, so disclosure methods for future releases may change.
doc_evidence: Fetched CBP methodology page (coverage, noise since 2007, 2017 publication rule, NAICS vintages) and the 2020 county record layout (fields and noise flags).
sample_evidence: cbp23co.zip (12.9 MB, 1,100,961 rows): Lake County IN (18089) all industries EST = 10,566; EMP = 171,790 (flag G); AP = 9,818,562 ($1,000).

name: Statistics of U.S. Businesses (SUSB)
description: Annual firms, establishments, employment (week of March 12) and payroll by enterprise employment size and NAICS industry; receipts in years ending in 2 and 7.
access_requirements: None; files about 5-53 MB.
time_coverage: Annual from 1997 (some tables from 1992); latest 2022 (released 2025)
history_notes: NAICS vintage changes; receipts only in years ending in 2 and 7.
suppression_rules: Noise flags on employment, payroll and receipts (EMPLFL_N, PAYRFL_N, RCPTFL_N; e.g., G, H).
limitations: Enterprise size reflects the whole firm nationally, not the local establishment; county detail limited to 3-digit NAICS; lagged.
doc_evidence: Fetched SUSB About page: firms, establishments, March 12 employment and payroll by enterprise size for U.S., states, MSAs, counties and congressional districts.
sample_evidence: Range request of us_state_6digitnaics_2022.txt: U.S. total FIRM = 6,395,635; ESTB = 8,298,562; EMPL = 135,748,407 (flag G).

name: Annual Business Survey (ABS): company summary
description: Employer firms, sales/receipts, employment and payroll by owner sex, race, ethnicity and veteran status, and by firm age and size; survey-based.
access_requirements: Census API key (project adapter).
time_coverage: API reference years include 2022 and 2023 (verified); 2024 not available as of 2026-09-28
history_notes: 2023 data use NAICS2022 codes; owner-characteristic categories may change between years.
suppression_rules: Relative standard errors published (FIRMPDEMP_S, RCPPDEMP_S, EMP_S, PAYANN_S); withheld-cell rules not reviewed.
limitations: Sample survey; owner-demographic detail is sparse for small areas; employer firms only.
doc_evidence: Fetched ABS API metadata: variables.json (FIRMPDEMP, RCPPDEMP, EMP, PAYANN, SEX, RACE_GROUP, ETH_GROUP, VET_GROUP) and geography.json (us, state, county, MSA, CD).
sample_evidence: Census API requires a key; verified by project adapter

name: Nonemployer Statistics (NES)
description: Annual counts and receipts of businesses with no paid employees (mostly self-employed individuals) by NAICS industry, from administrative tax records.
access_requirements: None for bulk files (under datasets/{year}/historical-datasets/); Census API key for the API.
history_notes: NAICS vintage changes; Connecticut planning regions in the 2023 county file.
suppression_rules: ESTAB_F and RCPTOT_F 'S' = suppressed (4,710 rows in the 2023 county file); RCPTOT_N_F noise flags G, H, J.
limitations: Counts businesses (tax filings), not people or jobs; receipts carry noise.
doc_evidence: Fetched NES API variables.json (NESTAB, NRCPTOT, NRCPTOT_N, NAICS2022) and geography.json (us, state, county, MSA, CSA).
sample_evidence: nonemp23co.zip (4.4 MB, 701,010 rows; ST, CTY, NAICS, ESTAB, RCPTOT): Lake County IN all sectors 34,461 establishments; receipts 1,590,444 ($1,000).

name: Business Formation Statistics (BFS): annual business applications by county
description: Annual counts of business applications by county (county file), alongside the monthly national BFS series.
access_requirements: None; single XLSX (sheet 'County Data'; header in row 3: State, County, County Code, state_fips, county_fips, BA2005-BA2025).
time_coverage: 2005-2025 annual county data (released 2026-06-10)
history_notes: Connecticut: 8 counties 2005-2021 and 9 planning regions 2022-2025 (blank outside each span); the June 2026 release used differentially private geometric noise; later releases are to follow Commerce DAO 216-26.
suppression_rules: Differentially private noise in the 2026 release; no cell suppression observed.
limitations: Applications are not business starts or employer births; noise matters for small counties; large 2020-2021 increases (e.g., Lake County IN 4,503 in 2019 vs 7,796 in 2020).
doc_evidence: Fetched BFS county page: 2005-2025 county data released June 10, 2026; differentially private noise note; DAO 216-26 statement.
sample_evidence: bfs_county_apps_annual.xlsx (526 KB): Lake County IN (18089) BA2019 = 4,503; BA2020 = 7,796; BA2025 = 6,991.

name: Business Dynamics Statistics (BDS)
description: Annual firm and establishment counts, establishment entry and exit, job creation and destruction and reallocation rates from the Longitudinal Business Database, for nation, states, counties and metros with firm age and size tabulations.
access_url: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/bds/tables/time-series/2023/bds2023_st_cty.csv (18 MB; sector, age and size variants 52-262 MB); API: https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/bds
access_requirements: None for CSV; Census API key for the API.
history_notes: Industry coded to 2017 NAICS in the API; county geography per release.
suppression_rules: API carries flag variables (_F) for cells; flag values not reviewed here.
limitations: Employer businesses only; rates use the DHS denominator (DENOM); small counties can be volatile.
doc_evidence: Fetched BDS API variables.json: ESTABS_ENTRY_RATE, ESTABS_EXIT_RATE, JOB_CREATION_RATE, NET_JOB_CREATION_RATE, DENOM (DHS denominator), NAICS (2017).
sample_evidence: Range request of bds2023_st_cty.csv: 27 columns (year, st, cty, firms, estabs, emp, denom, estabs_entry_rate, ...); first row 1978 Autauga AL estabs = 430.

name: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES 8): workplace and residence area characteristics
description: Annual job counts by 2020 census block of workplace (WAC) and residence (RAC) by NAICS sector (CNS01-CNS20), worker age, monthly earnings band and, from 2009, race, ethnicity, education and sex; OD files link home and work blocks.
access_requirements: None; gzip CSV per state (Indiana WAC 2023: 1.2 MB); aggregate blocks with {st}_xwalk.csv.gz.
time_coverage: 2002-2023 for most states
history_notes: LODES8 uses 2020 census blocks; demographic variables only 2009+; firm age and size (WAC, private jobs) 2011+; federal jobs (OPM) added from 2010.
suppression_rules: Disclosure avoidance applied (not reviewed here); some states lack OD/WAC files in some years.
limitations: Counts jobs, not people; earnings bands use fixed nominal thresholds ($1,250 and $3,333 per month) in every year; job-type choice (JT00 all jobs vs primary jobs) changes totals.
doc_evidence: Fetched LODES Technical Document 8.4: file naming, WAC/RAC layouts (C000, CE01-CE03, CNS01-CNS20), coverage 2002-2023 for most states.
sample_evidence: in_wac_S000_JT00_2023.csv.gz (1.2 MB, 52,088 blocks): Lake County IN (18089) block sum of C000 = 191,504 jobs.

name: Quarterly Workforce Indicators (QWI)
description: Quarterly employment, hires, separations, turnover, job flows and average monthly earnings by industry, worker sex/age, race/ethnicity, education and firm age/size for states, counties and metros, from LEHD administrative data; workplace-based.
access_requirements: None; files are large (e.g., 103 MB gzip for one Indiana county-by-sector file); the QWI API on api.census.gov needs a key.
